title: Figure 1: Cold fusion power densities vs. temperature, significant experimental data
description: Chart titled "Power Densities - Significant Experimental Data" plotting "Power Density (Kw/cc)" (0 to 9) against "Temperature (°C)" (0 to 1000), with an upward curve and labeled boxes for D2O electrolysis results, SRI, F&P (Fleischmann & Pons), molten salt electrolysis, "Life After Death" boil dry, and F&P "Ignition" boil dry (sample melted at 1554°C). A dashed line marks the "Minimum power density for commercial applications." The caption reads "Figure 1. Based on nothing but experimental data, this shows that to get several Kw/cc we need to be operating at temperatures above about 600°C"; the page is from a BAASS paper dated Nov-08, with names redacted under 1843(a)(2).
